items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, Early 1970s
items.q: I mean, of course, a lot of the great guys came out of New Orleans, like Louis Armstrong, and King Oliver, and Buddy Petit...

ctx.x: So it's pretty high. You know, we've had a number of people on the show, and we've talked to them about jazz, or swing, or big bands, or whatever you want to call it. And it would seem to me that you would be the man that would know the origin of such terms as jazz. Because you were born originally down there in the Crescent City itself, weren't you?

Yeah, I was born in New Orleans, and they say that's where jazz was born. I mean, of course, a lot of the great guys came out of New Orleans, like Louis Armstrong, and King Oliver, and Buddy Petit, and Buddy Bolden, Lorenzo Teo, Piku, Alphonse Piku. What was the first group? And the Andrei, and people like that.
What was the first group you worked with?
